limitations: This is deterministic automated screening, not a professional security audit. It does not execute the contract or prove economic safety.
Address bits prove which callbacks PoolManager is allowed to route, not that a pool currently uses this hook or that every callback succeeds.
Imported and inherited behavior is covered only when those source files were included in the analyzed bundle.
Runtime role holders, pool liquidity, swap volume, LP fees, and complete callback history require pool-aware indexed or onchain reads beyond this request.
cannotSee: It reads code and chain state; it never runs the hook, fuzzes it or simulates a trade against it.
Findings are fixed rules over verified source; with no verified source it sees only the callback bits and the bytecode.
A score is a screen, not an audit: logic bugs, price manipulation and economic attacks across contracts can pass it.
Code the hook calls at run time (another contract, an upgrade behind a proxy after this read) is outside the read.
Pool usage counts can be partial; a pool's own settings are read only with poolId on hookr_pool.
